name: comparator-transient-noise
description: Input-referred noise floor of the WHOLE comparator (comparator_dut, the real regenerative latch, NOT comparator_dut_analog), measured by transient-noise decision statistics (a 'hit-rate' / probit measurement) over the full PVT grid -- the compliance evidence path DR-0002 names, per CLAUDE.md's 'input-referred noise floor from transient-noise runs with seeds and run counts committed'. The injected trnoise() source is calibrated to the SPECTRAL DENSITY of comparator-preamp-noise's own input-referred white noise (36.27 nV/rtHz at the nominal corner), NOT to that bench's band-limited integrated total -- the latch's own aperture, not the reduced sub-model's bandwidth, then sets the noise bandwidth that reaches the decision.
claim: sim/dut.json binds design/comparator.spice (id comparator-dr0001, provenance schematic), the ratified topology from spec/decision-records/0001-comparator-topology.md ('DR-0001'). This record substantiates a TRNOISE-injected, decision-statistics sweep over the full PVT grid against the WHOLE latch (comparator_dut, real CLK strobe, real regenerative pair): at each PVT point it measures the probability of a correct decision at +/- a fixed differential overdrive, from which an input-referred 1-sigma decision noise follows by probit inversion (see this experiment's README.md). It is NOT itself the README.md#target-specification Input-referred-noise row ratification act (that is spec/porting-plan.md's separate third step; DR-0002 ratified the SCOPING of the row and names transient noise as its compliance evidence path). Unlike comparator-preamp-noise/'s .noise analysis, this bench exercises the ACTUAL regenerative loop -- no loop-broken reduced sub-model, no small-signal DC-operating-point assumption, and no reliance on that sub-model's own noise bandwidth. It remains a LOWER BOUND on the complete figure in one specific, stated way: the DUT's black-box pin contract lets this deck inject noise only at vinp/vinn, so the regenerative pair's own noise sources are not independently sourced (see the notes below).
analyses: meas tran vsup_v find v(vdd) at=0.5n
meas tran d0now find v(dout0) at=5n
meas tran d1now find v(dout1) at=5n
meas tran d2now find v(dout2) at=5n

frac_high_zero.description: NOISE-IS-ACTUALLY-INJECTED GUARD, not a spec bound. At zero applied overdrive, zero mismatch (the plain mos corner set), the ONLY thing that can make a trial decide either way is the injected trnoise() realization -- so frac_high_zero should sit near 0.5 (binomial SEM at N=80 is ~5.6% at p=0.5). If trnoise() ever failed to inject (e.g. a regression that zeroed vn_na), the zero-overdrive rung would instead decide the SAME way on EVERY trial, collapsing frac_high_zero to 0.0 or 1.0 -- well outside this floor/ceiling. THIS IS NOT AN ASSUMPTION, IT WAS RUN: with vn_na forced to 0 at tt_27c_1.20v this deck returns frac_high_zero = 2.3e-8 (LOW on every trial), frac_high_plus = 1.0 and frac_high_minus = 2.3e-8, and this check FAILS as designed -- see this experiment's README.md 'Negative control (actually run)'. THIS IS ALSO THE HARNESS'S SABOTAGE-NEGATIVE-CONTROL SURROGATE FOR THIS BENCH: --sabotage-corners forces every corner to plain mos_tt (sim/harness/corners.py), which does not itself disable trnoise() the way it disables mismatch for comparator-offset-mc/, so this check's real teeth are structural (a broken or zeroed noise source), not sabotage-corner-specific.

frac_high_plus.description: SANITY ENVELOPE, not a spec bound. At +od_x (1.0 mV, deliberately chosen near the measured 1-sigma decision noise so the hit rate lands in the informative 0.7-0.95 band rather than saturating) the correct decision is HIGH, so frac_high_plus should sit above 0.5. The floor is loose (0.3) so N=80 sampling variance cannot fail an otherwise-fine point, while still catching a badly broken or inverted-polarity deck (frac_high_plus stuck near 0 across the WHOLE grid). The ceiling is 0.999, not 1.0, on purpose: a saturated frac_high_plus = 1.0 carries no information about sigma (the probit inversion of p=1 is infinite, so sigma would read as exactly 0), so saturation is a measurement failure for this bench and must fail the check rather than silently produce a flattering number.

frac_high_minus.description: SANITY ENVELOPE, symmetric with frac_high_plus above: at -od_x the correct decision is LOW, so frac_high_minus (the fraction deciding HIGH, i.e. INCORRECTLY) should sit below 0.5. Ceiling loosened to 0.7 for the same N=80 sampling-variance reason; the 0.001 floor is the mirror of the 0.999 ceiling above -- a saturated frac_high_minus = 0 inverts to an infinite probit and a sigma of exactly 0, which is a measurement failure, not a pass.

evidence.mc_seed: ngspice `setseed 20260916` at the top of the control block (the same literal seed value comparator-offset-mc/ uses, and the same `setseed` form testbench.py's record_kind='monte-carlo' loader guard requires, per issue #28's agauss()/`set rndseed=` finding). RUN COUNT: N=80 trials per rung per PVT point, via `reset` inside a `dowhile` loop -- each reset genuinely re-draws a new TRNOISE realization. SEED REPRODUCIBILITY DOES NOT HOLD FOR THIS MECHANISM, unlike comparator-offset-mc/'s agauss() draws: `setseed`, `set rndseed=` and `.option seed=` were each tested independently (this experiment's README.md 'Seed reproducibility') and NONE of them reproduces identical TRNOISE draws across separate ngspice invocations on this repo's pinned ngspice-46 (sim/toolchain.json) -- TRNOISE's internal generator is not tied to the RNG stream any of those three commands controls. The seed is therefore RECORDED, NOT LOAD-BEARING; what is load-bearing, and is committed, is the run count (N=80 per rung per point, common across the whole 45-point grid) together with the frac_high_* values observed on this specific dated run. A re-run of the identical deck samples a DIFFERENT set of draws and lands at a statistically consistent but not bit-identical frac_high_*. N for statistical-error purposes is 80 per rung per point, not 80 x 45.
evidence.mc_scope: SPECTRAL-DENSITY CALIBRATION, NOT TOTAL-RMS CALIBRATION -- and this distinction is the methodological core of this bench. The trnoise() source injects a white differential voltage whose ONE-SIDED spectral density equals comparator-preamp-noise's own INPUT-REFERRED white density at the nominal corner: 36.27 nV/rtHz = white_nv_rthz / av_dc = 59.4598 / 1.63936 (record 20260916-113303-180cca7). vn_na = 5.735e-3 solves vn_na*sqrt(2*vn_ts) = 36.27e-9 at vn_ts = 20 ps, using the TRNOISE density relation S_1sided = vn_na*sqrt(2*vn_ts) V/rtHz -- derived analytically AND confirmed empirically on this pinned ngspice-46 (this experiment's README.md 'NA/TS calibration'). Calibrating to that bench's INTEGRATED TOTAL instead (277.827 uV rms) would be wrong here: that total is integrated over the reduced sub-model's OWN 58.7 MHz noise bandwidth, whereas the quantity this bench measures is set by the LATCH's own aperture -- a bandwidth the reduced sub-model has no say in. Matching the total rather than the density would understate the injected in-band density by the ratio of those bandwidths. The SAME injected density is used at EVERY PVT point (deliberately not re-derived per corner), isolating what this bench adds -- how THIS corner's own regeneration dynamics convert a GIVEN input noise density into a decision-boundary sigma -- from the front end's own already-corner-characterized noise magnitude, the same separation-of-concerns comparator-regeneration/ and comparator-offset-mc/ already make for delay and offset.
evidence.mc_sigma: Implied 1-sigma input-referred decision noise, by the standard probit inversion of a hit-rate measurement: sigma = od_x / Phi^-1(frac_high_plus) from the +od_x rung and sigma = od_x / Phi^-1(1 - frac_high_minus) from the -od_x rung, with od_x = 1.0 mV and Phi^-1 the standard-normal inverse CDF. This assumes the decision is a threshold-at-zero comparison of (overdrive + noise), which holds here because mismatch is off on this corner set. It is a POST-HOC calculation over this record's frac_high_plus/frac_high_minus columns, not an in-deck measurement (see the notes below for why the deck emits no sigma_uv). PRECISION IS NOT A FLAT PERCENTAGE, unlike a linear quantity's SEM: the binomial SEM on frac_high (~5.6% at p=0.5 for N=80, smaller at the tails) propagates through Phi^-1's derivative, which is steep near p=0.5 and shallow in the p~0.7-0.95 band the od_x choice puts these rungs in -- so a SINGLE corner's implied sigma carries roughly +/-20% of sampling scatter, and the two rungs at the SAME corner (which would agree exactly at infinite N) disagree by correspondingly more. Quote the GRID-WIDE MEAN across all 45 corners x 2 rungs as the summary statistic; per-corner extremes are sampling-dominated. The exact spread observed on any given record is reported in this experiment's README.md 'Records', not asserted here, because a re-run resamples it.
notes: THIS MEASURES DECISION STATISTICS (a hit-rate / probit measurement), NOT A PSD INTEGRAL. frac_high_zero/plus/minus are the raw, directly observed quantities; the conversion to an implied 1-sigma input-referred noise is a documented, reproducible post-hoc calculation over this record (this experiment's README.md 'Probit inversion'). The deck deliberately emits no sigma_uv measurement: a saturated frac_high of exactly 1.0 makes the probit inversion singular, and ngspice's `let` has no clamp to guard it with -- the frac_high_plus/frac_high_minus checks above fail on saturation instead.

WHAT THIS ADDS OVER comparator-preamp-noise/ (DR-0002's reportable lower bound). That bench's `.noise` analysis is a small-signal, DC-operating-point analysis of comparator_dut_analog, DR-0001's diode-connected, loop-broken reduced sub-model: it structurally excludes the regenerative loop's dynamics, and -- just as importantly -- its integrated total is band-limited by that sub-model's own 58.7 MHz noise bandwidth, which is not the bandwidth over which a real strobed decision integrates noise. This bench instantiates the WHOLE comparator_dut (real CLK strobe, real cross-coupled regenerative pair), injects the SAME input-referred noise DENSITY, and lets the real latch set its own aperture. That is why the sigma reported here is LARGER than the AC bench's integrated total: the AC number is a genuine lower bound (fewer noise sources AND a narrower band), exactly as DR-0002 frames it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ADD. This deck injects noise ONLY at comparator_dut's contract input pins (vinp/vinn) -- the DUT's black-box pin contract (sim/dut/README.md) gives testbenches no access to internal nodes, so the regenerative pair's OWN thermal/flicker noise sources cannot be independently injected without editing design/comparator.spice (out of this issue's scope). The injected density is itself the reduced sub-model's input-referred white density, so the front-end term inherits that model's own limits. The result is therefore 'the front end's own noise density, propagated through the real regeneration dynamics and the real aperture' -- materially more complete than the AC bench's number, but still a lower bound on the complete figure, not a certificate.
MISMATCH IS OFF (the plain mos corner set). Offset (comparator-offset-mc/) and noise are separate terms budgeted separately -- unchanged convention from the other three benches.

SOLVER TOLERANCES ARE LOOSER than the other three benches' (reltol=1e-2/abstol=1e-12 here vs 1e-4/1e-9/1e-13 there) -- deliberately: this bench only needs a correct BINARY decision at a fixed readout instant, not the sub-picosecond delay precision comparator-regeneration/'s tau extraction needs, and looser tolerances materially cut the cost of the N x 3-rung x 45-corner transient-run grid this bench needs (vs. those benches' single tran/dc call per point).
